gap: Character surface fidelity. In the 1280x720 frame with the man 2-3 m away, a crop of his face must show skin breakup (stubble shadow, pores or specular variation), defined eyelids with eye highlights and at least forehead or nasolabial creasing that gives a readable expression. The shirt must show several modelled, self-shadowed fold lines at the shoulders, elbows and waist, not a flat plaid shell. Forearms must have a tapered wrist and anatomical volume, and the hand holding the prop must curl around it.

- GTA V images were only resized in my scratchpad and written as B.jpg in the pair dirs. None went into progress/.. Judge: B is clearly better in all four pairs, and none of the calls was close. The A frames in pairs 1-3 use one character asset on one arcade set, and the same failures show up each time. The character reads as a mannequin: smooth uniform tan skin, shell hair with a sawtooth fringe, thin tube arms without elbow anatomy, stiff splayed paddle hands and props that are not really gripped. The plaid texture is good, but the cloth has no fold geometry. The set is empty and sterile: repeating tile, blank sign plates, plants sprouting from the tiles, and bloom-heavy strip lights that never light the subject, so the 'daytime' shots look dim and directionless. Pair 4 A, the street shot, is the most promising A frame. Its dappled sun under rain trees, shophouse frontage and skyline give it a real sense of place, but it has only about five pedestrians, a flat placeholder building on the left, visibly repeating paving and a blank-grid minimap. The B frames win on character fidelity (expressive detailed faces, folded layered cloth, hands that interlock with their props), on story and density (fire and a jerry can, a bat, a crowded Walk-of-Fame-style boulevard) and on lighting with clear intent (hard sun, moonlit snow against stained glass, neon night). One caveat: the B frames in pairs 1-3 look like staged, posed hero captures, so part of the gap is direction and composition, not raw engine rendering. Even so, character head and hand fidelity, correct grip and aim poses, cloth folds and pedestrian density are the main gaps the A game has to close.
